title: Splitting a geometrically diagonalizable group over a separably closed field
statement: Let $k$ be a separably closed field [def-weil-field, def-kun-separably-closed], and let $E/k$ be an extension field [def-pc-field-extension] with $E$ algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $H$ be an affine group scheme of finite type over $k$ [pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A group scheme is a group object in schemes over its base; a group isomorphism preserves multiplication, identity and inverse. For a commutative ring $R$ and a finitely generated additive abelian group $N$, write $D_R(N)=\operatorname{Spec}R[N]$ with the group-algebra Hopf operations of [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. Suppose $H\times_k E\simeq D_E(N_0)$ as $E$-group schemes for some finitely generated abelian group $N_0$, where scalar extension uses fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then there exist a finitely generated additive abelian group $N$ and an isomorphism $D_k(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}H$ of $k$-group schemes. Neither algebraicity of $E/k$ nor smoothness, connectedness or reducedness of $H$ is assumed; torsion in $N_0$ is allowed.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, opening paragraph of B.4, printed p.297 (arbitrary field-extension independence), and Lemma B.1.5, printed pp.283-284 (finite separable splitting); combined separably closed instance. Online source read; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this group-scheme result.

proof.text: Let $K\subseteq E$ consist of the elements algebraic over $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-relative-algebraic-closure-algclosed], $K$ is an algebraic closure of $k$, even when $E/k$ is transcendental. Put $C=k[H]$. The affine group coordinate theorem [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf] identifies $H$ with $\operatorname{Spec}C$ with its actual Hopf operations. The affine fibre-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] gives $H_K=\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_kC)$ and $(H_K)_E\simeq H_E$: the ring identification sends $a\otimes(b\otimes c)$ to $ab\otimes c$, with inverse $a\otimes c\mapsto a\otimes(1\otimes c)$. These maps respect multiplication, coproduct, counit and antipode on pure tensors. The same fibre-product formula shows $H_K$ is affine, and [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](2) makes it finite type over $K$.

source.place: Tags 09GJ (lemma-algebraic-permanence), 09GR (lemma-algebraically-closed), 09GS (definition-algebraic-closure); affine base-change formula: schemes.tex Tag 01I4; finite type: morphisms.tex Tag 01T4.

proof.text: Choose generators $n_1,\ldots,n_r$ of $N_0$ as an abelian group. The surjection $\mathbf Z^r\to N_0$ gives the surjective algebra map $E[\mathbf Z^r]\to E[N_0]$, $e_a\mapsto e_{\sum_i a_i n_i}$: each target basis monomial has a preimage. The group-algebra formulas in [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group] show on basis elements that this map preserves coproduct, counit and antipode. By [lem-sfb-hopf-spectrum-functor] and the affine criterion in [def-weil-closed-immersion], its spectrum is a closed group embedding $D_E(N_0)\hookrightarrow D_E(\mathbf Z^r)$. Compose with the given isomorphism $H_E\simeq D_E(N_0)$. The finite-type and torus assertions of [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-group-geometric-criteria] give $D_K(\mathbf Z^r)\simeq\mathbf G_{m,K}^r$ of finite type over $K$. The maps $E\otimes_K K[\mathbf Z^r]\rightleftarrows E[\mathbf Z^r]$, $a\otimes(be_m)\mapsto ab e_m$ and $a e_m\mapsto a\otimes e_m$, are inverse Hopf algebra maps. Together with [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], they identify $(D_K(\mathbf Z^r))_E$ with $D_E(\mathbf Z^r)$. Hence we have a closed group embedding $(H_K)_E\hookrightarrow(D_K(\mathbf Z^r))_E$. For $N_0=0$ take $r=0$.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(a), printed pp.233-234; explicit group-algebra monomial surjection and scalar extension.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-algclosed-group-embedding-existence-descent] over the algebraically closed field $K$ with extension $E/K$, source $H_K$ and target $D_K(\mathbf Z^r)$. Both groups are affine and of finite type by steps 1 and 2, and step 2 supplies the required closed group embedding after scalar extension. We obtain a closed $K$-group embedding $H_K\hookrightarrow D_K(\mathbf Z^r)\simeq\mathbf G_{m,K}^r$. Thus $H$ satisfies exactly the definition in [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality]: its extension to the algebraic closure $K$ of $k$ is a closed subgroup of a finite product of multiplicative groups. The descended embedding need not extend to the originally chosen embedding over $E$; only its existence is used.

source.place: Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), parts (2),(3), with algebra.tex Tag 00FV (theorem-nullstellensatz), as assembled in the existing embedding-existence-descent node. Conrad Appendix B.4, printed p.297, uses the same specialization route.

proof.text: Apply the finite separable splitting assertion of [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality] to $H/k$. The original hypotheses give an affine group of finite type, and step 3 verifies multiplicative type over an algebraic closure of $k$. We obtain a finite separable field extension $L/k$, a finitely generated additive abelian group $N$, and an isomorphism $H_L\simeq D_L(N)$ of $L$-group schemes. No smoothness or reducedness condition enters this theorem, so torsion in $N_0$ causes no restriction.

source.place: Corollary 12.19, printed p.238; finite separable splitting also stated in Conrad Lemma B.1.5, printed p.283.

proof.text: Since $k$ is separably closed, [lem-pc-sepclosed-finite-sep-trivial] makes the finite separable extension $L/k$ trivial. Restricting the splitting of step 4 along the inverse $k$-algebra identification $L\simeq k$ gives $H\simeq D_k(N)$; the scalar maps on coordinate tensors send $a\otimes c$ to $ac$ and $a e_m$ to $a e_m$. They preserve each group operation by its scalar-extension formula. Invert this group isomorphism to get the required $D_k(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}H$. In particular this also covers the trivial group and nonreduced diagonalizable groups such as $\mu_p$ in characteristic $p$.

source.place: Corollary 12.19, printed p.238, specialized to a separably closed field.
